stops.name: Copenhagen, the exile household
stops.campa: In Copenhagen the exiles make a household. Reich trains Danish students, among them Philipson and Leunbach, writes, and begins the descent from the word into the flesh: the work that will be called vegetotherapy is conceived in these rooms, and the canon is clear about its second parent. Elsa, trained by Laban and Gindler, is the somatic knowledge in the house; she begins studies of her own that will found her later art. Denmark watches the scandalous doctor, and the visa is a candle burning from both ends.

stops.name: Malmö, across the Sound
stops.campa: Denmark declines to renew the doctor's visa: psychiatrists complain, a newspaper savages, the Danish Party expels a man who never joined it. The household moves three miles across the Sound to Malmö. Exile becomes geometry: the Danish students ferry over on alternate days for their training, and Elsa ferries back, several days a week, to keep her dance work alive in Copenhagen. In the boarding-house between two hostile shores, the two of them keep a school of the future.

stops.name: Berlin, Christmas among the endangered
stops.campa: At the turn of the year Elsa goes back into Germany, into the Reich itself, to see family and friends in Berlin, while Reich circles Europe testing London, Paris, Zurich and the Tyrol. The visit is quietly heroic: her name stands in police files, and the city she posters against now rules itself by warrant. In Berlin the lovers meet again in passing and travel north together to Malmö. She will keep returning to the city that wants her arrested, as if Berlin were a wound that must be personally inspected.

stops.name: Malmö, the watched boarding-house
stops.campa: Malmö is a big village and the village is watching: a secret-service agent is set on the boarding-house where Reich and Elsa live, students are intercepted at the ferry and taken to police headquarters for questioning, and the Danish and Swedish police coordinate their zeal. In April, on the same day as a raid on Philipson's house in Copenhagen, Reich's room is searched without a warrant. Nothing is found and no charge is ever raised, but the residence permit dies of it. The Sound closes; they must vanish for a summer.

stops.name: Sletten, the incognito summer
stops.campa: They spend the early summer illegally in Denmark, in the fishing village of Sletten on the Øresund coast, Reich under a false name and Elsa keeping the small house of the vanished. The sea, the boats, the herring-smoke: the two most watched bodies in Scandinavia rest by lying still. In hiding the work goes forward: the vegetative currents, the breath, the musculature of fear, argued out nightly between a doctor with a theory and a dancer with the thing itself.

stops.name: The camp by the lake, honeysuckle and free bodies
stops.campa: In August they drive south across Europe, camping, with Reich's daughters, an idyll the canon preserves in Eva's memory: dancing with Elsa, the smell of honeysuckle all around them, free bodies exercising, bathing in the lakes, Reich tender with Elsa as Eva had rarely seen him with her own mother. By the water near Lucerne the caravan halts. For one summer the family that could not exist, exists: assembled from exiles, and held together by a dancer.

stops.name: Lucerne, the congress casts him out
stops.campa: At the Thirteenth International Psychoanalytic Congress in Lucerne the guild completes what the states began: Reich is maneuvered out of the International Psychoanalytic Association, hears his case judged in rooms he is not admitted to, and delivers his scheduled lecture as an outcast. Elsa watches the man she crossed borders for come back from the halls a saddened man. Church and Party have both cast him out now; what remains to him is the body, and the woman who knows how it speaks.

stops.name: Oslo, Drammensveien 110h, the new beginning
stops.campa: By November they are living together at Drammensveien 110h in Oslo, called north by the psychologist Harald Schjelderup to the last radical capital of Europe. Reich will write it later like scripture: Drammensvejen, the new beginning. Here vegetotherapy is built in daily sessions and nightly arguments, and the canon names the era the golden age of body psychotherapy: Reich with the character-analytic theory, Elsa with the somatic art, Raknes and Hoel and the Norwegians gathered round. The city knows her as his second wife, unwed and unashamed.

stops.name: Berlin, the child not born
stops.campa: In the new year Elsa is carrying Reich's child, and she is overjoyed; then his doubts set in, the work too unsettled, the future too provisional, and to her great sorrow he insists. She travels to Berlin, where Edith Jacobson of the resistance helps arrange the illegal operation, and in a city ruled by the enemy the child of the dancer and the doctor is not born. Reich writes to her in Berlin that he loves her deeply and wants children with her. The canon lets the wound stand, unhealed and unexplained.

stops.name: Oslo, the return in March
stops.campa: In March she returns to Oslo and to work, and the account settles into a rare word for this life: happy. The three years from the fall of 1934 are, the chronicle says, among the happiest of Reich's life, and Elsa is the reason. He supports her independence in principle and mostly in practice; she builds a career of her own beside his, not inside it. In the evenings the household above the fjord fills with seminars, dancers, analysts and refugees. The north is kind for a season.

stops.name: Oslo, the workers' stage
stops.campa: The workers' stage takes her: Elsa is engaged with the Arbeiderteatret, choreographing for the red revues at the Arbeidersamfundet: agitprop made flesh, the Berlin street-theatre nights reborn in Norwegian. From 1935 to 1939 she works the workers' theatre while teaching dancers on her own account. The exiled corps-dancer of the Städtische Oper now sets miners' sons and shop-girls moving in formation, and the movement choir of Laban's doctrine discovers what it was always for.

stops.name: Oslo, the seminars: ballet changed into Reichian movement
stops.campa: In her Oslo studio Elsa teaches movement that is no longer exactly dance: ballet changed, her students say, into Reichian ways of moving: breath, pulse, the armor found and melted in the muscle. Young Gerda Geddes, in analysis with Raknes, takes lesson after lesson and stands, she will say, at the front of an avant-garde. This is the canon's cradle of dance-movement therapy: a dancer with Gindler's ear and Laban's geometry, applying the psychoanalyst's map of resistance to bodies in motion.
